muc.title: How good is AI?
muc.text: AI has finished learning. But how do we know how good it is? Every ad brags: our new AI scored 90%. Where does that number come from?

muc.title: AI takes tests too
muc.text: AI takes tests too, like students taking final exams. AI's tests are called benchmarks: thousands of questions with answers ready, and every AI gets the same test.

muc.title: The score is the percent correct
muc.text: Grading is simple: compare AI's answers with the answer key. Get 900 out of 1,000 right, and the score is 90%.

muc.title: A test for each subject
muc.text: Some tests cover knowledge in many subjects, from history and medicine to law. Some are math tests, solved step by step. Some are coding tests: AI writes code, and a computer runs it to see if it works.

muc.title: One test, one skill
muc.text: But each test measures only one skill. Getting an A in math doesn't mean you write well. An AI that's great at coding tests may not write good emails.

muc.title: 90% on which test?
muc.text: So 90% on one test can't be compared with 90% on another. The number only means something when you know what the test is.

muc.title: Ask two questions back
muc.text: Next time you see an ad saying an AI scored 90%, ask two questions. What was the test about? And is that like what I usually ask AI to do?

muc.title: What if AI saw the test first?
muc.text: But what if AI saw the test before taking it? Can you still trust a high score? See you in part 2.
